# Orbit

> Mind maps written in markdown and explored like a solar system. The node in focus is the sun, its children orbit it as planets and their children are moons; readers click a planet to fly into it, zoom, and flick the orbit to spin it. Framework-agnostic and dependency-free, with a web component, React and marked integrations, SVG export without a browser, and a command line.

- Install with `npm install @restless-dreams/orbit`. The package is ESM-only. React (`@restless-dreams/orbit/react`) and marked (`@restless-dreams/orbit/marked`) are optional peers.
- A map fills its container: always give the container a height.
- Write maps in orbit-md, Orbit's markdown (every heading and list item is a node, text under it is its note, `<!-- orbit key: value -->` comments set attributes), or in YAML (`nodes:` with `text` and `children`).
- Check a map with `npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate --json map.md`: every problem comes with a suggested fix, and its line where it has one. `npx @restless-dreams/orbit example` prints a map with the main features, and `orbit convert --to yaml map.md` (or `--to md`) turns one flavor into the other.
- Draw one with `createOrbitMap(element, markdown, options)`, the `<orbit-map>` element, `<OrbitMindMap source={markdown} />` from `@restless-dreams/orbit/react`, or `renderToSVGString(markdown, options)` without a browser.
- Share a map as one web page, which opens in any browser, offline: `npx @restless-dreams/orbit export --html map.md --out map.html`.
- Let people build the map on the map with `editable: true` (a + in the orbit, text typed inside nodes), and save what they make with `map.toMarkdown()` on the `edit` event.
- Let a language model read and change a map with `createMapTools(map)`: `tools.for('anthropic' | 'openai' | 'openai-chat' | 'gemini')` lists the tools for its API, and `tools.run(name, input).text` is each call's result.
- Maps speak the page's language (`lang`): English and Spanish are built in, `registerLanguage` adds more.
- Themes: `paper` (default), `night`, `glass`, `glass-night`, `cosmos`, `blueprint`, `ink`, `contrast`, `flat`, `flat-night`, `material`, `material-night`, `liquid`, `liquid-night`, `auto`. Pass `theme: 'night'` or `theme: { preset: 'night', tokens: { … } }`, or set `--orbit-*` CSS custom properties.

## Docs

- [Map format](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/format.md): headings, lists, notes, media, every attribute and document option, the YAML flavor, and every diagnostic code
- [README](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/README.md): install and a quick start for each way to draw a map
- [Guide](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/guide.md): every renderer option, event and method, the React component, the element, marked, pictures and videos, SVG export and the command line
- [Recipes](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/recipes.md): plain HTML, React and Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Astro, remark and rehype, static sites
- [Theming](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/theming.md): the fourteen themes, Material themes from any color, and every CSS custom property
- [Extending](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/extending.md): node types, your own actions, status words and named themes, for one map or every map
- [Editing](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/editing.md): context menus on a long press, adding, renaming, moving and removing nodes on the map, and saving the result as orbit-md
- [Map tools for AI](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/map-tools.md): tools for any model to read and change a map, on screen or on a server, for each provider's API and MCP
- [Languages](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/languages.md): maps in the page's language, English and Spanish built in, adding languages and changing single words
- [Pictures and videos](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/media.md): the media viewer, its keys, YouTube and Vimeo, sound and autoplay, and opening, playing and following media from code
- [Coding agents](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/agents.md): the skill, validation as JSON, and messages for setup mistakes
- [Everything in one file](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@restless-dreams/orbit/llms-full.txt): the README and all of the guides above, for the latest release
- [Website](https://orbit.hyuchia.com): live examples, the themes side by side, setup for each integration, and a playground to write a map and explore it in the browser

## Optional

- [Accessibility](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/accessibility.md): keyboard, screen readers, reduced motion and contrast
- [API reference](https://github.com/restless-dreams/orbit/blob/main/docs/api/README.md): every export, generated from the types

<!-- README.md -->

<img src="docs/media/logo.svg" alt="Orbit's logo: a golden sun with six colorful planets on a dotted orbit" width="96">

# Orbit

Mind maps written in markdown and explored like a solar system.

![A map of a product roadmap: the orbit spins, the camera flies into a branch and out to the overview of the whole map](docs/media/tour.webp)

**[Website](https://orbit.hyuchia.com)** · [Playground](https://orbit.hyuchia.com/playground) · [Guide](docs/guide.md) · [Map format](docs/format.md) · [Recipes](docs/recipes.md) · [Theming](docs/theming.md) · [Extending](docs/extending.md) · [Editing](docs/editing.md) · [Map tools for AI](docs/map-tools.md) · [Pictures and videos](docs/media.md) · [Languages](docs/languages.md) · [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md) · [Coding agents](docs/agents.md) · [API reference](docs/api/README.md)

- Real-markdown authoring: headers and bullet lists nest the tree.
- YAML alternative for app-generated maps.
- Explorable: zoom into a node to enter it and out to leave, flick the orbit to spin it, pan and zoom the overview. Every move is animated so you never lose your place.
- Readable at any size: labels stay crisp, sized for reading and in high contrast.
- Fourteen themes, from pastel paper and a field of stars to flat, Material and liquid glass, each restylable with CSS custom properties, and Material themes built from any color.
- First-class pictures, videos, embeds and multi-line notes per node: pictures and videos open over the whole window, to zoom into and to play, and the rest in a built-in detail sheet, unless you handle `onAction` yourself.
- Built on the map: a + in the orbit adds ideas, typed right inside their planet, and nodes can be renamed, dragged and saved back as markdown.
- Ready for AI: tools any model calls to read a map and change it, for Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, MCP and the providers that follow OpenAI's API, with every change animated on the map.
- Keyboard and screen-reader friendly: one tab stop, arrow-key navigation, a list view of the whole map, and announcements as you move, in English, Spanish or any language you add.
- Framework-agnostic core with no dependencies; React wrapper at `@restless-dreams/orbit/react`; `marked` extension at `@restless-dreams/orbit/marked`.
- Made for coding agents too: the docs in one file (`llms-full.txt`), an agent skill, validation as JSON, and problems reported with the fix.

## Install

```bash
npm install @restless-dreams/orbit
```

React and marked are optional peers, needed only for their integrations: `npm install react react-dom` for `@restless-dreams/orbit/react`, and `npm install marked` for `@restless-dreams/orbit/marked`.

## Quick start

```ts
import { createOrbitMap } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

const map = createOrbitMap(document.getElementById('map')!, `# 🚀 Project

## Research
## Build
## Launch`);

map.on('focus-change', ({ node }) => console.log('Now looking at', node.text));
```

The map fills its container, so give the container a size.

**React:**

```tsx
import { OrbitMindMap } from '@restless-dreams/orbit/react';

export const ProjectMap = ({ markdown }: { markdown: string }) => {
  return (
    <div style={{ height: 480 }}>
      <OrbitMindMap source={markdown} onNodeClick={(node) => console.log(node.text)} />
    </div>
  );
};
```

**Without a build step,** with the `<orbit-map>` element:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { defineOrbitMapElement } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@restless-dreams/orbit/+esm';
  defineOrbitMapElement();
</script>

<orbit-map height="420">
  # 🚀 Project

  ## Research <!-- orbit status: active -->
  ## Build
</orbit-map>
```

**In a markdown pipeline,** with marked:

```ts
import { Marked } from 'marked';
import { orbitMarked, hydrateOrbitBlocks } from '@restless-dreams/orbit/marked';

const markdown = new Marked(orbitMarked());
container.innerHTML = await markdown.parse(article); // orbit fences become map placeholders
hydrateOrbitBlocks(container);                         // turns them into live maps
```

**Without a browser,** `renderToSVGString(markdown, { width: 1200, height: 800 })` draws a standalone SVG, for static sites, emails and print.

[The guide](docs/guide.md) covers every option, event and method, and [Recipes](docs/recipes.md) shows Orbit in Vue, Svelte, Astro, Next.js and static sites.

## Write a map

Every heading and every list item is a node, the text under it is its note, and `<!-- orbit … -->` comments set attributes:

```markdown
---
title: Product roadmap
theme: night
---
# 🚀 Product roadmap

## Research <!-- orbit status: done -->
Six weeks of interviews before we commit to scope.
- [x] User interviews
- Competitor teardown #market

## Build <!-- orbit status: active -->
### Frontend
- [/] App shell
- Offline sync
### Backend

## Launch
![The launch poster](images/poster.png)
```

Maps can be YAML too, for the ones programs write. [The map format](docs/format.md) has every rule, attribute, option and diagnostic, and `npx @restless-dreams/orbit example` prints a map with the main features.

## Themes

![The fourteen themes: paper, night, glass, glass night, cosmos, blueprint, ink, contrast, flat, flat night, material, material night, liquid and liquid night](docs/media/themes.webp)

Pick one with the `theme` option, the `theme` attribute or `theme:` in the frontmatter. Every color, size and finish is a CSS custom property your page can set, and `materialTheme('#0B57D0')` builds a Material theme from any color. See [Theming](docs/theming.md).

## Command line

```bash
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate my-map.md                  # every problem as my-map.md:line: severity: message [code]
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate --json my-map.md           # the same as JSON, for scripts and coding agents
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate --tree my-map.md           # the map as Orbit reads it, with each node's id
npx @restless-dreams/orbit render my-map.md --out my-map.svg   # draw a map to SVG (--view all for the whole map)
npx @restless-dreams/orbit export --html my-map.md --out my-map.html  # one web page to explore or present the map, offline
npx @restless-dreams/orbit convert --to yaml my-map.md         # markdown ↔ YAML (either direction)
npx @restless-dreams/orbit example > my-map.md                 # a map with the main features (--yaml for YAML)
```

## AI in your app

`createMapTools(map)` gives a language model tools to read the map and change it, in the shape your provider's API takes. Its changes animate on the map, and a call it gets wrong changes nothing and says what to send instead:

```ts
import { createMapTools } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

const tools = createMapTools(map);   // a map on screen, or a document on a server
tools.for('anthropic');              // the tools for the model: also 'openai', 'openai-chat' and 'gemini'
tools.run('add_nodes', { parent_id: 'research', outline: '- Interviews\n- Survey' });   // each call it makes: { ok, text, changed }
```

[Map tools for AI](docs/map-tools.md) has the whole loop for each provider.

## Coding agents

Point your agent at `node_modules/@restless-dreams/orbit/llms-full.txt`, the docs in one file, or install the skill for Codex, Claude Code, Kimi Code and other agents with `npx skills add restless-dreams/orbit`. [Coding agents](docs/agents.md) has the details.

## Browsers

Orbit is made for current browsers, and draws in older ones down to Chromium 99, which some phones' WebViews still run, with plainer versions of the few effects that need newer CSS ([which ones](docs/guide.md#browsers)).

## Contributing

With [Bun](https://bun.sh) installed, `bun install`, then `bun run verify` runs the linter, the type checks, the tests and the build. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the rest, [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md) how releases are made, and [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) how Orbit is put together.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

<!-- docs/guide.md -->

# Using Orbit

How to draw maps on any page, in React, with the `<orbit-map>` element or in a markdown pipeline, and everything a map offers: its options and events, how people move around it, pictures and videos, editing, export and theming. [The map format](format.md) is the reference for writing maps, and [Recipes](recipes.md) shows Orbit in each framework.

## Drawing a map

```ts
import { createOrbitMap } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

const map = createOrbitMap(document.getElementById('map')!, `# 🚀 Project

## Research
## Build
## Launch`);

map.on('focus-change', ({ node }) => console.log('Now looking at', node.text));
```

The map fills its container, so give the container a size. `createOrbitMap` returns the renderer: call `map.render(newMarkdown)` to draw a new version (the reader keeps their place), and `map.destroy()` when you remove it. Options passed in win over the document's frontmatter; `documentToRendererOptions(doc.options)` shows what a document asks for. `new OrbitSVGRenderer(element, options)` plus `renderer.render(source)` is the same thing in two steps.

## React

```tsx
import { OrbitMindMap } from '@restless-dreams/orbit/react';

const markdown = `# Project

## Research
## Build`;

export const ProjectMap = () => {
  return (
    <div style={{ height: 480 }}>
      <OrbitMindMap source={markdown} onNodeClick={(node) => console.log(node.text)} />
    </div>
  );
};
```

`OrbitMindMap` fills its parent, so give the parent a size. Pass the map as `source` (markdown or YAML), as a parsed `document`, or as a node tree in `data`. Inline callbacks and inline `theme` / `palette` objects are fine: the map only redraws when their values change.

- **Drive it from code** with a ref: `ref.current.flyTo(id)`, `overview()`, `setViewMode(mode)`, `zoomBy(factor)`, `fit()`, and `ref.current.renderer` for everything else.
- **Control the focus** with `focusedId` and `onFocusChange`, like a controlled input.
- **Server rendering:** the component is marked `"use client"` for React Server Components. On the server and in the first render it draws a static SVG of the map, so the page shows it before JavaScript runs; the live map replaces it on mount (`staticFallback={false}` turns that off).

## Web component

```ts
import { defineOrbitMapElement } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';
defineOrbitMapElement();
```

```html
<orbit-map height="420" view-mode="focus">
  # 🚀 Project

  ## Research <!-- orbit status: active -->
  ## Build
</orbit-map>
```

Indent the content however you like, and `<!-- orbit … -->` comments and frontmatter work inside the element. The map renders in a shadow root, so the raw markdown is never shown. You can also put the source in a `<script type="text/orbit">` child or a `source` attribute.

- **Size:** the element is a block, 420 px tall by default. Use the `height` attribute, `height` in the frontmatter, or plain CSS (`orbit-map { height: 60vh }`, which wins over both).
- **Attributes:** `view-mode`, `theme`, `palette` (comma-separated), `max-depth`, `interactive`, `animation`, `editable`. Changing one updates the map in place.
- **Updates:** editing the element's content or its `source` property redraws the map, and the reader keeps their place. `element.flyTo(id)` and `element.overview()` move the map, `element.openMedia(id)` shows a node's picture or plays its video (see [Pictures and videos](#pictures-and-videos)), and `element.renderer` is the underlying `OrbitSVGRenderer`.
- **Events:** the map's events bubble out of the element (see Events below).
- **Errors:** a map that can't be drawn shows an error card with the line number and fires an `orbit-error` event (`event.detail.message`, `.line`, `.diagnostics`).

To avoid a flash of raw markdown before the script loads, hide undefined elements: `orbit-map:not(:defined) { visibility: hidden; }`.

## Markdown pipelines (marked)

```ts
import { Marked } from 'marked';
import { orbitMarked, hydrateOrbitBlocks } from '@restless-dreams/orbit/marked';

const markdown = new Marked(orbitMarked());
container.innerHTML = await markdown.parse(article); // orbit fences become map placeholders
hydrateOrbitBlocks(container);                         // turns them into live maps
```

Fences can carry display options: ```` ```orbit height=480 theme=glass view=all ````. Each map fills its placeholder, which is 420 px tall unless the fence's `height` or the map's frontmatter says otherwise; CSS that gives the placeholder a height wins over both. Until a placeholder hydrates (or when JavaScript is off), it contains a nested list of the map, so the content stays readable and indexable. `renderOrbitMarkdown(markdown)` renders with a private instance in one call; `configureMarked(instance)` registers the extension on an existing instance (the global `marked` by default). Neither touches the global `marked` unless you pass it.

## Format

Orbit reads two flavors: orbit-md, its markdown, and YAML. The dispatcher (`parseOrbit`) tells them apart. [The map format](format.md) has every rule, attribute, option and diagnostic; `npx @restless-dreams/orbit example` prints a map that uses all of them.

### orbit-md, the markdown flavor (recommended for maps people write)

Every heading and every list item is a node; everything else belongs to the node above it. Headers (`#`–`######`, or lines underlined with `===` and `---`) nest by level, and every list under a heading is its children, as deep as you indent. Checkboxes set a status: `- [ ] Draft` is `todo`, `- [x] Ship` is `done`, `- [/] Build` is `active`. Hashtags at the end of a title are tags: `- Offline sync #frontend`.

A document can also be just a list. A single top item becomes the root; with several, the root is named after the frontmatter `title`, a one-line paragraph above the list, or "Untitled map". Several `#` headings share a root the same way:

```markdown
Project plan
- Research
- Build
- Launch
```

```markdown
# 🚀 Project Launch

## Research
- Market analysis
- User interviews

## Build

### Frontend
### Backend

## Launch
```

Image, video, and embed:

```markdown
## Mountain Trip

![Sunrise from the summit](photos/sunrise.jpg)

We left at 5am to catch the sunrise.
```

Text under a heading or a list item is its note: paragraphs, quotes, code. The
list after it is still the children. Under a list item, indent the note, a
picture or an attribute block, as you would under a heading. To keep a bullet
list inside a note, quote it with `>`:

```markdown
## Build
Currently focused on the frontend. Starts when [Research](#research) is done.

- Frontend <!-- orbit status: active -->
  Vite + React. Ships behind the beta flag.
- Backend
  ![Backend diagram](diagrams/backend.png)
  > - Billing
  > - Search

## Research
```

A `#id` link, like `[Research](#research)` above, flies to that node of the map.

Per-node attributes go in HTML comments that start with `orbit`. Other comments are hidden, as markdown hides them:

```markdown
## Build
<!-- orbit
color: "#F5A3A8"
status: active
priority: 1
tags: [frontend, sprint-3]
-->
```

Document-level frontmatter sets renderer options:

```markdown
---
view: focus
palette: ["#F8D978", "#F5A3A8", "#A8DDB5"]
baseUrl: /docs/assets/
---
# Project
```

### YAML flavor (for app-generated maps)

```yaml
title: My Project
view: focus
nodes:
  - text: Project
    icon: 🚀
    children:
      - text: Research
        tags: [discovery]
        children: [Market analysis, User interviews]   # scalar shorthand
      - text: Build
        status: active
        note: |
          Currently focused on the frontend.
          Targeting end-of-quarter ship.
```

Plain strings in `children` are shorthand for `{ text: ... }` leaf nodes.

### Document options

Frontmatter (markdown) or top-level keys (YAML): `title` (used as the SVG's
accessible label), `view`, `theme`, `showRings`, `interactive`, `animation`,
`speed`, `palette`, `height`, `maxDepth` (levels below the root to render;
`1` = root + direct children), `className`, `baseUrl`, `schemaVersion` (the
format version the document is written for, `1`). Keys Orbit doesn't know are
kept and written back, and saving keeps a file as it was written: only the
ideas an edit changed are written again (see
[What saving keeps](format.md#what-saving-keeps)).

### Problems in a document

Parsing is forgiving. When something is wrong but recoverable (an unknown frontmatter key, a second `#` root, an attribute block that isn't valid YAML, an image without a URL), the parser works around it and records a diagnostic with a code, the line it's on and a message that says how to fix it (`Unknown frontmatter key "rings" (ignored). Did you mean "showRings"?`):

```ts
const doc = parseOrbit(source);

for (const problem of doc.diagnostics ?? []) {
  console.log(problem.line, problem.code, problem.message);
}
```

Pass `{ strict: true }` to throw an `OrbitParseError` (with `code` and `line`) on the first problem instead. `orbit validate` lists every problem and fails until there are none. When a map rendered through `<orbit-map>` or `renderOrbitMarkdownBlocks` can't be drawn at all, it shows an error card and dispatches an `orbit-error` event; the other maps on the page still render.

### Round-tripping

`serializeOrbitMarkdown` / `serializeOrbitYAML` produce documents that parse back to the same tree. The markdown reads the way people write maps:
- **Headings and lists:** the root and its children are headings, and everything below them is a nested list.
- **Titles:** statuses on list items are checkboxes (`[ ]`, `[/]`, `[x]`) and simple tags are hashtags; titles are escaped only where markdown would misread them.
- **Attributes:** short ones go on the node's line, `<!-- orbit color: "#E8A33D", priority: 2 -->`: up to three, or more while the comment stays under 80 characters (`<!-- orbit type: goal, target: 5, current: 2, unit: apples -->`). The rest go in a comment block below it.
- **Notes and media:** notes are plain paragraphs, quoted only when their lines would read as nodes, and pictures and videos are lines of their own.

A map written in that style comes back unchanged.

```ts
import { parseOrbit, serializeOrbitMarkdown, serializeOrbitYAML } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

const doc = parseOrbit(source);
const asYaml = serializeOrbitYAML(doc);
const backToMarkdown = serializeOrbitMarkdown(parseOrbit(asYaml));
```

## Action API

Wire your own behavior on click:

```ts
const renderer = new OrbitSVGRenderer(host, {
  onAction: ({ node, action }) => {
    if (action === 'image') {
      openMyLightbox(node.image!.src);
    }

    if (action === 'note') {
      openMyDrawer(node.note!);
    }

    return false; // skip Orbit's own viewer and detail sheet
  },
});
```

The focused node shows a button for each kind of content it has, then your own [actions](extending.md#actions). They sit under it, or, where its planets crowd it (as they do on a phone), under the whole orbit, which is then fitted to leave them room: they never cover a planet. When `onAction` isn't provided (or doesn't return `false`), "View image" and "Play video" open the [media viewer](#pictures-and-videos), and the other buttons the built-in detail sheet: a panel along the right edge on wide screens and a bottom sheet on phones (swipe down to close), with the node's media, note, status and tags, and arrows to step through its siblings. YouTube and Vimeo links play through their embeddable players (`youtube-nocookie.com/embed/…`, `player.vimeo.com/video/…`). Links open in a new tab.

Notes are markdown and are rendered safely (no raw HTML). Opt-out flags: `showActionButtons: false`, `showDetailSheet: false` and `mediaViewer: false`. Custom note rendering: `noteRenderer: (note, ctx) => '<p>...</p>'`. The HTML it returns is used as is, so sanitize it if the note content is untrusted.

## Pictures and videos

"View image" and "Play video" open the media viewer, over the whole window, even when the map sits in a small box. It follows the map's theme, light or dark.

- **Pictures** fit the window. The wheel, a pinch, a double click or tap, the `+`, `−` and `0` keys and the zoom buttons zoom around the point under the pointer, and a zoomed picture pans with a drag.
- **Videos** start at once: files in the browser's own player, YouTube and Vimeo in theirs.
- **Every picture and video of the map,** in reading order: the previous and next buttons, the arrow keys or a swipe step through them, and a counter says where you are.
- **Around them,** the node's title, the caption and the picture's description, with a link to the picture or to the video's page. Esc, a click around the media or a swipe down closes the viewer, and focus goes back where it was.

The detail sheet's picture opens the viewer too, and its video has a button that moves it there. `mediaViewer: false` keeps pictures and videos in the detail sheet, and `onAction` returning `false` (or the `action` event's `preventDefault()`) skips both, as for any button.

A page can drive the viewer itself, to show a picture big or play a video on a screen of its own, such as an audience's while someone presents:

```ts
map.openMedia('summit');                                    // a node's picture, or its video
map.openMedia('trail', { kind: 'video', autoplay: false }); // its video, ready to play
map.openMedia('trail', { kind: 'video', startAt: 42 });     // its video, playing from 0:42
map.playMedia();
map.seekMedia(42);
map.pauseMedia();
map.unmuteMedia();                                          // from a press, for a video a browser started muted
map.closeMedia();
map.on('media-state', ({ node, playing, time }) => tellThePresenter(node.id, playing, time));
```

`openMedia` works whatever `mediaViewer` and `showDetailSheet` say. On a map that isn't interactive, the viewer is the page's to drive: no buttons, no video controls, and no input of its own. [Pictures and videos](media.md) covers the keys, YouTube and Vimeo, sound and autoplay, and the events.

## Extending

Give nodes a type, add your own buttons, name your own themes and status words. Pass them to one map, or register them once for every map, `<orbit-map>` elements and markdown pages included:

```ts
import { createOrbitMap, registerTheme } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

registerTheme('brand', { preset: 'night', tokens: { 'color-root': '#FFD166' } });

createOrbitMap(element, '# Launch\n## v1.0 beta <!-- orbit type: milestone, status: review -->', {
  theme: 'brand',
  nodeTypes: {
    milestone: { label: 'Milestone', icon: '🏁', color: '#F59E0B', details: (node, element) => { element.textContent = 'Due Friday'; } },
  },
  actions: [{ id: 'assign', label: 'Assign', icon: '👤', run: (node) => openAssignDialog(node) }],
  statuses: { review: 'active' },
});
```

A node type sets its nodes' icon, color and theme tokens, can draw inside them (`render`), add a section to the detail sheet (`details`) and bring its own actions. `nodeTypeFor` gives nodes that name no type one to be drawn as, for display only: it's never written to the map. [Extending](extending.md) covers every option.

## Editing on the map

Let people build a map on the map itself. With `editable`, a **+** in the orbit adds an idea, typed right inside its new planet. Enter adds it and opens the next one, so ideas go in one after another. A long press, a right click or F2 edits a node's text where it is, and a node held still lifts, to be dragged onto another node or to a new place in the orbit:

```ts
const map = createOrbitMap(element, markdown, {
  editable: true,
  onEdit: () => save(map.toMarkdown()),
});
```

With `editingKeys` too, the keyboard builds maps as in mind-map apps: Tab adds an idea under the node with keyboard focus, Shift+Enter beside it, and Delete removes it; while typing, Tab and Shift+Tab go a level down and up.

For a menu of your own, `onNodeContext` reports the long press or right click and where it happened, and `onNodeDrag` when the press moves on to drag the node, the moment to close the menu. `editNode(id)`, `editNewNode(parentId, index?)`, `addNode`, `updateNode`, `removeNode` and `moveNode` then change the map, animating each edit and firing `edit`. `toMarkdown()` writes the edited map as orbit-md. [Editing](editing.md) covers menus, dragging, keys, ids, focus, saving, React and `<orbit-map editable>`.

## Interaction

A map has two views. **Focus** puts one node at the center (the sun) with its children around it (planets) and their children as small moons. The **overview** lays out the whole tree.

- **Moving around:** click or tap a planet (or a moon) to fly into it; click the sun, the back chip or a breadcrumb to go back up. The camera flies between views along a smooth zoom path, and nodes that both views share move into place.
- **Zooming:** the wheel, a trackpad pinch or a two-finger pinch zooms around the pointer. In focus mode, zooming into a planet enters it once it's big enough to read, so a crowded orbit can be zoomed into and read first; zooming out leaves the current node, and a small zoom out springs back. The overview zooms and pans freely, with momentum.
- **Spinning:** drag around the sun to turn the orbit. A hard flick keeps it spinning and slowing down like a fidget spinner; a touch catches it. `spin: { snap: 'planet' }` brings the nearest planet to the top as it stops, and `onSpinSettle` tells you which one.
- **Pages that scroll:** when the page around the map scrolls, the wheel scrolls the page and Ctrl (⌘ on a Mac) + wheel zooms the map; on touch screens, one finger scrolls the page except on the orbit itself. `zoom: { wheel: 'always' }` or `'modifier'` changes this.
- **Keyboard:** the map is one tab stop. In focus mode, `←`/`→` step through the planets (turning the orbit so the chosen one is on top), `↓` enters the orbit, `↑` returns to the sun, `Enter`/`Space` flies into a node, `Escape`/`Backspace` goes back. In the overview, the arrow keys follow the tree. `+`, `−` and `0` zoom and fit.
- **Assistive technology:** the list button shows the whole map as a nested list, which screen readers can also browse at any time, and moves are announced. When the reader asks for reduced motion, views cross-fade instead of flying and a flicked orbit doesn't coast.
- **Pictures and videos:** "View image" and "Play video" open them over the whole window, to zoom into a picture (the wheel, a pinch, a double click or tap) and to play a video; the arrows and swipes step through every picture and video of the map. See [Pictures and videos](#pictures-and-videos).
- **Editing:** on `editable` maps, the + in the orbit adds an idea and a long press, a right click or F2 edits a node's text. A long press, a right click, or the context menu key (or Shift+F10) also fires `node-context`, for a menu of your own. A node held still lifts: drag it onto another node to move it there, or along the orbit to a new place. With `editingKeys`, Tab, Shift+Enter and Delete add and remove ideas from the keyboard. See [Editing on the map](#editing-on-the-map).
- **Programmatic:** `renderer.flyTo(id)` (in focus mode), `renderer.overview()`, `renderer.focusNode(id)` (keeps the current view), `renderer.setViewMode(mode)`, `renderer.zoomBy(factor)`, `renderer.fit()`, `renderer.spin(degreesPerSecond)`, `renderer.getFocusPath()`, `renderer.getFocusedNode()`, `renderer.getViewMode()`, `renderer.getNodeColor(id)` for the color a node is drawn with, to match a list or legend beside the map, and `renderer.openMedia(id)`, `closeMedia()`, `playMedia()`, `pauseMedia()`, `seekMedia(seconds)` and `unmuteMedia()` for the media viewer.

## Events

Listen on the renderer, or for DOM events that bubble from the map's container (and out of `<orbit-map>`):

```ts
const stop = map.on('focus-change', ({ node, path }) => {});
element.addEventListener('orbit-focus-change', (event) => event.detail.node);
```

| Event | DOM event | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `focus-change` | `orbit-focus-change` | `{ node, path }`: the focused node and the path from the root |
| `view-mode-change` | `orbit-view-mode-change` | `{ mode }`: `'focus'` or `'all'` |
| `node-click` | `orbit-node-click` | `{ node }`, before the map reacts |
| `action` | `orbit-action` | `{ node, action, sourceEvent }`; `preventDefault()` skips the built-in viewer, sheet or link |
| `spin-settle` | `orbit-spin-settle` | `{ planet }`: the planet on top when a spun orbit stops |
| `node-context` | `orbit-node-context` | `{ node, x, y }`: a long press, right click or context menu key on a node, and where; `preventDefault()` takes the press |
| `edit` | `orbit-edit` | `{ kind, node, tree }`: an edit, made on the map or with `addNode`, `updateNode`, `removeNode` or `moveNode` |
| `editor-open`, `editor-close` | `orbit-editor-open`, `orbit-editor-close` | `{ node, parent }`: the field for typing on the map opened or closed, on `node` or for a new idea under `parent` |
| `node-drag` | `orbit-node-drag` | `{ phase, node, parent, index }`: a node dragged somewhere else, as it leaves its place (`start`), when where it would go changes (`over`), and when it's let go (`end`) |
| `media-open`, `media-close` | `orbit-media-open`, `orbit-media-close` | `{ node, kind, index, total }`: the media viewer opened (or stepped) on a node's picture (`kind: 'image'`) or video, `index` of `total` in reading order, or closed |
| `media-state` | `orbit-media-state` | `{ node, playing, time, duration, ended, muted }`: the viewer's video started, paused, moved on, ended or was muted; while it plays, its time a few times a second |
| | `orbit-error` | `{ message, line, diagnostics }`, on elements whose map couldn't be drawn |

The `on…` options (`onFocusChange`, `onAction`, …) receive the same information.

## Server rendering and export

`renderToSVGString` draws a map without a browser, for static sites, emails, docs and print. Colors are resolved to plain values and labels are SVG text, so the file looks the same anywhere:

```ts
import { renderToSVGString } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

const svg = renderToSVGString(markdown, { width: 1200, height: 800, theme: 'night', viewMode: 'all' });
```

Options: `width` and `height` (positive, up to a million pixels), `viewMode`, `focus` (a node id), `theme`, `palette`, `maxDepth`, `showRings`, `title`, `baseUrl`, `responsive` (100 % wide and tall instead of pixels) and `idPrefix` (when several SVGs share a page). In the browser, `renderer.toSVGString()` exports what's on screen.

## A map as a web page

`orbit export --html` makes one HTML file with Orbit, the map and its pictures inside. It opens in any browser, offline: explore the map with Orbit's own controls, or present it, one idea at a time in reading order with its note as a caption (the Present button or P; the arrows, Space or a swipe step, Escape stops). It's the way to share a map for review: send the file to someone, or to your own phone.

```bash
npx @restless-dreams/orbit export --html map.md --out map.html --theme auto
```

Pictures on your computer that the map shows (its nodes' pictures, videos' thumbnails and pictures in notes) go inside the page; pictures on the web stay links, and so do videos. `--title`, `--theme`, `--view`, `--focus` and `--language` work as for `render`; with `--theme auto` the page follows the reader's light or dark mode.

In code, `exportWebPage` returns the same page. It needs Orbit's web page script, `@restless-dreams/orbit/web-page.js`, as text, to put inside:

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { exportWebPage } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

const script = readFileSync(new URL(import.meta.resolve('@restless-dreams/orbit/web-page.js')), 'utf8');
const html = exportWebPage(markdown, { script, theme: 'night', media: { 'photos/summit.jpg': 'data:image/jpeg;base64,…' } });
```

Options: `title`, `theme`, `viewMode`, `focus`, `language`, `strings` and `media`, the pictures to put inside the page by the address the map gives them.

## Map tools for AI

`createMapTools` gives a language model tools to read a map and change it: read it as an outline with each node's id, search it, add branches written as markdown, rename, mark, move, sort and remove nodes. `tools.for('anthropic')`, `'openai'`, `'openai-chat'` or `'gemini'` lists them in the shape that provider's API takes, `tools.definitions` as MCP lists tools, and `tools.run(name, input)` carries out each call. On a map on screen, each change animates and fires `edit`; on a document, it changes the document in place. A call a model gets wrong changes nothing, and its result says what to send instead. [Map tools for AI](map-tools.md) has the loop for each provider.

## Notes in your own UI

`renderNoteMarkdown` renders a note the way the detail sheet does, for a page that shows notes itself, such as captions under a presented map. It builds DOM nodes rather than HTML text, so a note can't add markup, and its links and pictures go through the same URL guard as the map:

```ts
import { renderNoteMarkdown } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

caption.replaceChildren(renderNoteMarkdown(node.note ?? '', { baseUrl }));
```

Options: `baseUrl`, where relative links and pictures resolve from, and `resolveLink(href)`, whether a `#id` link points at a node of the map (links to missing nodes show as plain text).

## Renderer options

| Option | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `viewMode` | `'focus'` | `'focus'` or `'all'` (the overview). |
| `focus` | the root | The node in focus when the map first draws, by id: to open a map where the reader left it. |
| `theme` | `'paper'` | A theme name (see Theming) or `{ preset, tokens }`. |
| `palette` | theme colors | Node colors: the first for the root, the rest cycle through the branches. |
| `maxDepth` | all levels | Levels below the root to draw. |
| `showRings` | `true` | Dashed orbit rings. |
| `interactive` | `true` | `false` draws a still picture. |
| `showControls` | `true` | Breadcrumbs, view switch, list button and zoom buttons. |
| `showActionButtons` / `showDetailSheet` | `true` | Content buttons under the focused node / the built-in detail sheet. |
| `mediaViewer` | `true` | Pictures and videos open in the media viewer, over the whole window; `false` keeps them in the detail sheet. |
| `editable` | `false` | A + in the orbit to add ideas, text edited inside nodes (long press, right click or F2), and nodes dragged somewhere else. |
| `editingKeys` | `false` | Mind-map keys on editable maps: Tab adds an idea under a node, Shift+Enter beside it, and Delete removes it; while typing, Tab and Shift+Tab go a level down and up. |
| `longPressDelay` | `500` | Milliseconds a touch holds still on a node before it is a long press; apps can pass their platform's own. |
| `insets` | | `{ top, right, bottom, left }` in px: the parts of the map your page covers with its own controls, such as a floating toolbar. Views are fitted into what's left, and the map still draws under them. |
| `orbitAnimation` / `orbitSpeed` | `false` / `90` | Let the orbit drift slowly, one turn every `orbitSpeed` seconds; it pauses while you point at it, tab through it, zoom or pan. |
| `spin` | | `{ decay: 1.4, maxSpeed: 1440, snap: false, haptics: false }`: seconds for a flick to lose two thirds of its speed, fastest spin in degrees per second, snapping a planet to the top, and a light vibration as planets pass the top. |
| `zoom` | | `{ wheel: 'auto', minimum: 0.4, maximum: 6 }`: wheel behavior and the zoom range relative to the fitted view. |
| `transitionDuration` | `'auto'` | Flight length in milliseconds, scaled to the distance travelled when `'auto'`; `0` turns flights off. |
| `ariaLabel` | document title | The map's accessible name. |
| `language` | the page's | The language of the map's buttons, sheets and announcements: a tag like `'es'` ([Languages](languages.md)). By default, the closest `lang` attribute around the map. |
| `strings` | | Words to change on this map only: `{ zoomIn: 'Closer' }`. |
| `baseUrl` | | Resolves relative image, video and link URLs. |
| `onNodeClick`, `onFocusChange`, `onViewModeChange`, `onAction`, `onSpinSettle`, `onNodeContext`, `onEdit`, `onEditorOpen`, `onEditorClose`, `onMediaOpen`, `onMediaClose`, `onMediaState` | | Callbacks. |
| `noteRenderer` | | Renders note markdown to HTML yourself. |

## CLI

```bash
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate my-map.md                  # every problem as my-map.md:line: severity: message [code]
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate --json my-map.md           # the same as JSON, for scripts and coding agents
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate --tree my-map.md           # the map as Orbit reads it, a node a line with its #id
npx @restless-dreams/orbit render my-map.md --out my-map.svg   # draw a map to SVG (--theme, --view, --focus, --width, --height, --language)
npx @restless-dreams/orbit convert --to yaml my-map.md         # markdown ↔ YAML (either direction)
npx @restless-dreams/orbit example > my-map.md                 # a map with the main features (--yaml for YAML)
npx @restless-dreams/orbit --version                           # the installed version
```

Use `-` as the file to read from stdin, and `--help` after any command for its options. `validate` exits with 1 while the map has a problem (`--loose` accepts the ones the map works around, but never a map it can't read); every command exits with 2 for a mistake in the command itself. `render` links pictures on your computer from where the SVG goes, so it can move with them. The command itself is `orbit`: where the package is installed, scripts can call `orbit validate my-map.md` directly.

## Languages

Maps speak the language of the page they're on: the buttons, the detail sheet, the media viewer and everything screen readers hear. English and Spanish are built in; `registerLanguage` adds others, and the `language` and `strings` options pick a language or change single words for one map.

```ts
import { createOrbitMap, registerLanguage } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

createOrbitMap(element, markdown, { language: 'es' });       // or <html lang="es">, or <orbit-map lang="es">
registerLanguage('fr', { zoomIn: 'Zoomer', overview: 'Vue d’ensemble' });
```

[Languages](languages.md) lists every word, and how to translate them.

## Theming

Pick a theme with the `theme` option, the `theme` attribute or `theme:` in the frontmatter:

![The fourteen themes: paper, night, glass, glass night, cosmos, blueprint, ink, contrast, flat, flat night, material, material night, liquid and liquid night](media/themes.webp)

- `paper` (the default): pastel planets with soft shadows, on your page's own background.
- `night`: planets that glow on a deep navy sky.
- `glass` and `glass-night`: frosted, translucent planets over a soft backdrop of their own.
- `cosmos`: jewel-toned planets around a golden star, in a field of stars.
- `blueprint`: outlined planets, construction lines and monospaced labels on a gridded blue sheet.
- `ink`: black line art with serif lettering, on your page's own background.
- `contrast`: black outlines, solid colors and bold labels, for the most legible map.
- `flat` and `flat-night`: solid, saturated planets with no shading, shadows or glow.
- `material` and `material-night`: Material 3's tonal containers and surfaces. `materialTheme('#0B57D0')` builds the same look from any color, the way Material You colors an app from its wallpaper.
- `liquid` and `liquid-night`: liquid glass, clear planets that catch the light along their rims, over a vivid wallpaper of their own.
- `auto`: `paper` or `night`, following the reader's light or dark preference.

Labels keep at least 4.5:1 contrast with their node in every theme.

Every color, size and finish is a CSS custom property, so you can restyle a map from your own stylesheet ([the full list](theming.md)). Properties set by the page win over the theme:

```css
orbit-map,
.my-map {
  --orbit-sans-font: Inter, sans-serif;  /* your font, in every sans-serif theme */
  --orbit-surface: #fbf8f3;              /* background behind the map */
  --orbit-color-root: #f8d978;           /* the root, then one color per branch */
  --orbit-color-1: #f5a3a8;
  --orbit-color-2: #a8ddb5;
  --orbit-node-text: #243042;
  --orbit-node-shadow-opacity: 0;        /* planets without a shadow */
  --orbit-ring-dash: none;               /* solid orbits */
  --orbit-sheet-background: #ffffff;     /* the detail sheet and the media viewer */
  --orbit-focus-ring: #2563eb;
}
```

Names are measured in the font they're drawn with, so they fill their nodes without spilling out of them, in any font, and fit again when a web font arrives ([Fonts](theming.md#fonts)).

The full list is exported as `THEME_TOKENS`, and `themeTokens(name)` returns a theme's values (for example to style your own UI to match). A `theme` object sets values in code (`theme: { preset: 'night', tokens: { surface: '#0b1020', 'ring-dash': 'none' } }`), and `palette: ['#…', '#…']` replaces the node colors. Children share their branch's color in lighter and darker shades, and labels switch to light text on dark nodes on their own.

## Browsers

Orbit is made for current browsers, and draws in older ones down to Chromium 99, which some phones' WebViews still run. A few effects need newer CSS, and older browsers get plainer versions instead of broken ones:

- without `color-mix()` (Chromium 111, Safari 16.2, Firefox 113), sibling ideas keep their branch's color instead of a shade of it, and rims, rings, shadows and halos take the theme's own colors;
- without the `translate` property (Chromium 104), overlays are centered through their transform;
- without the `dvh` unit (Chromium 108), the detail sheet sizes by `vh`.

## Cleanup

If you mount via `renderOrbitElement` and later remove the host from the DOM, call `OrbitSVGRenderer.unmount(host)` to release RAF + ResizeObserver resources. The `<orbit-map>` element does this automatically.

---

<!-- docs/format.md -->

# Map format

The complete reference for writing Orbit maps. A map is a tree: one root, and nodes with children. Write it in **orbit-md**, Orbit's markdown (the default, for maps people write), or in **YAML** (for maps programs write). `npx @restless-dreams/orbit example` prints a map with the main features, and `npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate map.md` checks one.

- [Markdown](#markdown)
  - [The tree](#the-tree)
  - [Node titles](#node-titles)
  - [Notes](#notes)
  - [Links between nodes](#links-between-nodes)
  - [Media](#media)
  - [Attributes](#attributes)
  - [Statuses](#statuses)
- [Document options](#document-options)
- [YAML](#yaml)
- [Which flavor a document is](#which-flavor-a-document-is)
- [Node ids](#node-ids)
- [Checking a map](#checking-a-map)

## Markdown

```markdown
---
title: Product roadmap
theme: night
---
# 🚀 Product roadmap
What ships this year.

## Research <!-- orbit status: done -->
Six weeks of interviews before we commit to scope.
- [x] User interviews
- Competitor teardown #market

## Build
### Frontend
- [/] App shell
- Offline sync <!-- orbit status: blocked -->
  Waits on the [backend](#backend) sync API.
### Backend

## [Launch](https://example.com/launch-plan)
![The launch poster](images/poster.png)
```

### The tree

**Every heading and every list item is a node.** Everything else belongs to the node above it.

- **Headings** (`#` to `######`) nest by level: a heading's children are the headings below it, up to the next heading at its own level or higher. A line underlined with `===` is a `#` heading, and with `---` a `##` heading. Headings may be indented up to three spaces and end with closing `#`s.
- **Lists** are children of the heading above them, every list, in the order written next to that heading's subheadings. Bullets (`-`, `*`, `+`) and numbered items (`1.`, `1)`) work the same. Indent an item further than the one above it to nest it under that item; lists go as deep as you like, past the six heading levels. A tab counts as four spaces.
- **The root** is the single top heading: the only heading at the highest level used, usually `#`. Several top headings share a root, as do the top items of a document that is just a list: it's named after the frontmatter `title`, a one-line paragraph above them, or "Untitled map". A list with a single top item is rooted at that item. Text before the root heading belongs to the root.
- A ```` ```orbit ```` or `~~~orbit` fence around the whole map is fine: `parseOrbit` unwraps it.

### Node titles

A heading's text, or a list item's first line, is the node's title, read in this order:

| Written | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `[ ] Draft` / `[x] Ship` / `[/] Build` | status `todo` / `done` / `active` |
| `🚀 Launch` (emoji first) | icon `🚀`, text `Launch` |
| `Offline sync #frontend #sprint-3` | tags `frontend` and `sprint-3`, text `Offline sync` |
| `Launch [plan](https://…)` | text `Launch plan`, link `https://…` |
| `**Frontend**`, `*Docs*`, `` `api` ``, `~~Old idea~~` | the text without the symbols |
| `Launch <!-- orbit status: active -->` | an attribute, inline (see [Attributes](#attributes)) |

- **Hashtags** count at the end of a title, after a space, and need a letter: `C# rewrite` and `Fix #42` stay as written.
- **Links:** a title that is all link works the same; with several links, the first is the node's link.
- **A backslash** keeps a character as written: `\*not bold\*`, `ship \#notatag`, `\[x] not a task`.

They combine: `## 📈 [Growth](https://example.com/growth) #q3 <!-- orbit status: active -->`.

### Notes

A note is longer text shown in the detail sheet, as markdown. Everything under a heading or list item that isn't a heading or list item is its note: paragraphs, `>` quotes, code blocks and tables.

- Under a list item, indent the note under it, as you would write anything under a heading. A line right after the item, with no blank line between, continues the item too.
- To keep a list inside a note, instead of making it children, quote it with `>`: headings and bullets inside a quote stay note text.

```markdown
# Launch
## Research
Questions to answer:
> - Who buys it?
> - Why now?

- Frontend
  Vite and React. Ships behind the beta flag.
- Backend
```

### Links between nodes

A link to `#id` points at another node of the map, the way `#heading` links point at headings in a page: a note link like `[Research](#research)`, or a node whose link is `#research`. It flies to that node instead of opening a page.

```markdown
# Launch
## Build
Starts when [Research](#research) is done.
## [Read the research](#research)
## Research
```

The id is the node's text in lowercase with dashes (see [Node ids](#node-ids)); `#Research` and GitHub-style `#-research` find it too. A link to a node the map doesn't have is reported.

### Media

A node shows its image (or its video's thumbnail) inside it. Its image and video open over the whole window, in the media viewer ([Pictures and videos](media.md)), and its embed in the detail sheet. Put each on a line of its own under the heading, or indented under the list item:

| Line | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `![Alt text](images/photo.jpg)` | the image |
| `[Trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=…)` | the video: YouTube, Vimeo, or a `.mp4`, `.webm` or `.mov` file |
| `[![Alt text](thumbnail.jpg)](https://vimeo.com/…)` | the video, with that thumbnail |
| `[Any other link](https://…)` | note text |

A node has at most one image, one video and one embed; extra media lines stay in the note. Embeds (a page shown in a frame) are set with the `embed` attribute. To read a media line differently, follow it with `<!-- orbit contentType: image -->` (or `video`, `embed`, or `none` to keep it as note text), and caption it the same way, with `<!-- orbit caption: The summit at dawn -->` right under it. Relative URLs resolve against `baseUrl`.

```markdown
# Trip
- Summit
  ![The summit at dawn](images/summit.jpg)
- Trail
  [Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aqz-KE-bpKQ)
```

Attributes set media too: `<!-- orbit image: images/photo.jpg -->`.

### Attributes

Attributes go in an HTML comment that starts with `orbit` (in any case, with or without a colon after it), written as YAML:

```markdown
## Build
<!-- orbit
color: "#F5A3A8"
status: active
priority: 1
tags: [frontend, sprint-3]
-->

- Frontend <!-- orbit status: active -->
- Backend
  <!-- orbit
  image: diagrams/backend.png
  note: Talks to the billing service.
  -->
```

- **Block form**: on the lines after a heading, or indented under a list item. Any number of keys. A block written right under a list item without its indent still belongs to the heading above the list, and an `attributes-after-list` note says so: indent it to set the list item's.
- **Inline form**: at the end of a heading or list item's line. Separate several with commas: `<!-- orbit status: active, priority: 1 -->`.
- **Other HTML comments** are hidden, as markdown hides them: Orbit keeps them in the file, out of titles, ids and notes as they're shown, and a renamed idea keeps the ones at the end of its title. One that reads like attributes but doesn't start with `orbit` (`<!-- status: done -->`) sets nothing, and a `comment-without-orbit` note says how to write it.

| Key | Value | Example | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | any CSS color | `"#F5A3A8"`, `tomato` | The node's color, instead of its branch's. Its children take shades of it. |
| `icon` | emoji or short symbol | `🚀`, `"★"` | Shown before the text. Same as an emoji at the start of the title. |
| `status` | text | `active`, `done`, `blocked` | Shown in the detail sheet; some words get a colored dot (see [Statuses](#statuses)). |
| `priority` | number | `1` | Shown in the detail sheet. |
| `tags` | list of text | `[frontend, sprint-3]` | Shown in the detail sheet. A single word works too, and so do words separated by commas: `tags: frontend, sprint-3`. Hashtags at the end of the title add to them. |
| `collapsed` | `true` / `false` | `true` | Hides the node's children (they show as a "+N" count) until you fly into it. |
| `link` | URL, or `#id` | `https://example.com` | Offered as a button when the node is in focus. Same as a link in the title. `#id` goes to another node (see [Links between nodes](#links-between-nodes)). |
| `note` | text | `Ships in May.` | The node's note. Same as a paragraph or blockquote. |
| `noteFormat` | `markdown` / `plain` | `plain` | How the note is shown. Default `markdown`. |
| `image` | URL, or `{ src, alt, caption }` | `images/photo.jpg` | The node's image. |
| `video` | URL, or `{ src, provider, thumbnail, caption }` | `https://youtu.be/…` | The node's video. `provider`: `youtube`, `vimeo` or `native`. |
| `embed` | URL, or `{ src, caption }` | `https://example.com/demo` | A page shown in a frame in the detail sheet. |
| `caption` | text | `The summit at dawn.` | Caption for the media line just above it, or for the one image, video or embed set next to it. Anywhere else, for the node's video, embed or image (in that order). |
| `id` | text | `launch` | The node's id, instead of one made from its text (see [Node ids](#node-ids)). |
| `type` | text | `milestone` | The node's type. A type your code defines sets its look, content and actions (see [Extending](extending.md#node-types)). Any case. |
| `contentType` | `image` / `video` / `embed` / `none` | `embed` | Markdown only: how to read the media line just above. |

Any other key is kept as a **custom attribute** in `node.attrs`, for your own code (`<!-- orbit owner: Ana -->`). A key that looks like a misspelled attribute (`colour`, `stauts`) is kept too, with a warning that suggests the right one.

### Statuses

`status` is free text, shown as written. These words (any case) also get a colored dot on the node and in the detail sheet:

| Dot | Words |
| --- | --- |
| active (blue) | `active`, `doing`, `in progress`, `wip`, `started`, `ongoing` |
| done (green) | `done`, `complete`, `completed`, `shipped`, `finished`, `closed` |
| blocked (red) | `blocked`, `stuck`, `at risk`, `failed` |
| todo (gray) | `todo`, `to do`, `planned`, `backlog`, `next`, `open` |

Other words get a neutral dot. Checkboxes set `todo` (`[ ]`), `done` (`[x]`) and `active` (`[/]`).

## Document options

Set in the frontmatter (markdown) or as top-level keys (YAML). Options passed in code win over these.

| Key | Value | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | text | the root's text | The map's accessible name and SVG title. Names the root when a document has no single top heading. |
| `theme` | `paper`, `night`, `glass`, `glass-night`, `cosmos`, `blueprint`, `ink`, `contrast`, `flat`, `flat-night`, `material`, `material-night`, `liquid`, `liquid-night` or `auto` | `paper` | See [Theming](theming.md). |
| `view` | `focus` or `all` | `focus` | The first view: one node with its children around it, or the overview of the whole tree. |
| `palette` | list of colors | the theme's | The root's color, then one per top-level branch, cycling. A comma-separated string works too. |
| `maxDepth` | number | all levels | Levels below the root to draw: `1` is the root and its children. |
| `showRings` | `true` / `false` | `true` | Draw the orbit rings. |
| `interactive` | `true` / `false` | `true` | `false` draws a still picture. |
| `animation` | `true` / `false` | `false` | Let the orbit drift slowly on its own. |
| `speed` | seconds | `90` | Seconds per turn of that drift. |
| `height` | pixels | `420` | Height of `<orbit-map>` elements and marked placeholders. |
| `baseUrl` | URL | | Resolves relative image, video and link URLs. |
| `className` | text | | Class names added to the map's element. |
| `schemaVersion` | number | | The version of the format the document is written for: `1`. See [Versions](#versions). |
| `flavor` | `markdown` or `yaml` | | Forces the flavor (see [Which flavor a document is](#which-flavor-a-document-is)). |

Flags also read `yes`, `no`, `on` and `off`.

## YAML

For maps that programs generate:

```yaml
title: Product roadmap
theme: night
nodes:
  - text: Product roadmap
    icon: 🚀
    note: What ships this year.
    children:
      - text: Research
        status: done
        children: [User interviews, Competitor teardown]
      - text: Build
        status: active
        children:
          - text: Frontend
            children:
              - App shell
              - text: Offline sync
                status: blocked
      - text: Launch
        link: https://example.com/launch-plan
        image: images/poster.png
```

- `nodes` is a list with the root node. Several top-level nodes share a root named after `title`, as in markdown.
- A node is a map with `text` and optionally `children`, plus any [attribute](#attributes) (`icon`, `color`, `status`, `link`, `note`, `image`, …) as a key. Custom keys are kept in `node.attrs`. A node without `text` but with `title`, `name` or `label`, or without `children` but with `items`, `nodes` or `subnodes`, is read with those as its text and children, and reported (`misnamed-node-key`) until they're renamed.
- A plain string in `children` is a node with just that text.
- Document options go at the top level, next to `nodes`.

## Which flavor a document is

`parseOrbit` reads a document as YAML when its frontmatter says `flavor: yaml`, its first line is `nodes:`, or the whole text reads as a YAML map: one with a `nodes:` list, or one that starts with a document option (`title:`, `theme:`, `view:`, …). Anything else is markdown, so a first line like `Status: draft`, or a note that starts with `nodes:`, stays markdown. `parseOrbitMarkdown` and `parseOrbitYAML` skip the detection.

## What saving keeps

Orbit never drops what a document says, even what it doesn't read:

- **Saving keeps the file as it was written.** `serializeOrbitMarkdown` (and a map's `toMarkdown()`) write a document parsed from markdown back line for line, and only the ideas an edit changed are written again: a renamed idea gets a new title line, a checked-off item a new checkbox, a moved idea takes its lines along. So a note written by hand or by another app keeps its formatting, its frontmatter keys, its HTML comments and rules, and its link definitions at the end. `{ keepSource: false }` writes the whole map in Orbit's own form instead; so does `orbit convert`.
- **Keys and values Orbit doesn't read are kept.** Frontmatter and top-level YAML keys it doesn't know are on `document.extra`, and both serializers write them back, with any changes an app makes to them: an app can keep a setting of its own there. A document without `extra` changes none of them, so no key another app wrote is lost; an `extra` object, even `{}`, changes or removes them. An attribute Orbit doesn't know is a custom attribute on `node.attrs`; a value it can't read for one of its own (a list for `status`, a word for `priority`) is reported and kept there under its own name. A picture or video keeps fields Orbit doesn't use (`width`, a `provider` it doesn't know).
- **A file that isn't a map yet** (only paragraphs) is a root with the text as its note: adding the first idea gives it a heading and keeps the text.

## Versions

A document says which version of the format it's written for with `schemaVersion`; none means `1`, the current one.

- **Older documents are upgraded as they're read.** When the format changes, Orbit brings documents written for the version before up to date as it reads them (a `format-upgraded` note says so), and the next save writes them as the new version, changing only what the upgrade changed.
- **Newer documents are read as well as they can be,** and reported with `unsupported-schema-version`, an error: apps should open them without letting them be edited. Nothing in them is lost by saving, but what this version doesn't know of them isn't understood either.
- **Node types have versions of their own,** for the fields their nodes keep in attributes: `type: task@2` says a node was written for version 2 of `task`, and none means 1. A type that changes its fields says so with `version` and brings older nodes up to date with `upgrade` (see [Extending Orbit](extending.md#versions)); a node written for a newer version of its type is left as it is.

## Node ids

Each node gets an id from its text: lowercase, accents folded, other letters kept (`Investigación` → `investigacion`, `研究` → `研究`, `Q3 plan` → `q3-plan`). Repeated ids get `-2`, `-3`, … in tree order. Set `id` to choose one; ids are what `renderer.flyTo(id)`, the `focus` export option and the React `focusedId` prop take.

## Checking a map

Parsing is forgiving: when something is wrong but the map can still be drawn, the parser works around it and records a diagnostic with a `code`, a `severity`, a message that says how to fix it and the `line` where it has one. `{ strict: true }` throws an `OrbitParseError` on the first one instead, except for the few that only note something and leave the map valid: `unknown-attribute` (kept as your own attribute), `synthetic-root`, `caption-without-media`, `format-upgraded`, `ignored-node-entry`, `comment-without-orbit` and `attributes-after-list`.

```bash
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate map.md          # every problem as map.md:line: severity: message [code]
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate --json map.md   # the same as JSON: valid, flavor, root, nodes, depth, diagnostics
npx @restless-dreams/orbit validate --tree map.md   # the map as Orbit reads it, a node a line with its #id
```

`validate` exits with 1 while the map has a problem that makes it invalid, and lists the notes too (add `--loose` to accept the problems the map works around, but never a map it can't read).

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `empty-document` | Nothing to draw. |
| `no-structure` | No headings or lists (markdown), or no `nodes:` list (YAML). |
| `synthetic-root` | Several top headings, items or YAML nodes and no title, so the root is called "Untitled map". |
| `invalid-frontmatter` | The frontmatter isn't valid YAML `key: value` pairs. |
| `unknown-frontmatter-key` | A frontmatter key Orbit doesn't know: kept and written back, but not used. The message names the one you probably meant. |
| `unknown-yaml-key` | The same, for a YAML document's top-level keys. |
| `invalid-option-value` | A document option with a value Orbit can't use, such as an unknown theme or a `flavor` other than `markdown` or `yaml`. |
| `unsupported-schema-version` | The document is written for a newer version of the format (an error: open it without editing it). |
| `format-upgraded` | The document was written for an older version of the format and read as the current one; saving writes it in the current one. |
| `invalid-attributes` | An attribute block isn't valid YAML, or a value has the wrong type: kept as written, but not used. |
| `unknown-attribute` | A key that looks like a misspelled attribute, kept as a custom one. |
| `media-missing-source` | An `image`, `video` or `embed` without a URL. |
| `unknown-content-type` | `contentType` isn't `image`, `video`, `embed` or `none`. |
| `caption-without-media` | A `caption` on a node with no image, video or embed. |
| `unknown-link-target` | A `#id` link points at no node of the map; the message suggests the id you probably meant. |
| `invalid-yaml` | The YAML document can't be read. |
| `ignored-node-entry` | A YAML node that is neither a map nor text. |
| `comment-without-orbit` | An HTML comment that reads like attributes (`<!-- status: done -->`) but doesn't start with `orbit`, so it sets nothing. |
| `attributes-after-list` | An attribute block right under a list item, without its indent: it sets the heading's attributes, not the item's. |
| `misnamed-node-key` | A YAML node's text under `title`, `name` or `label`, or its children under `items`, `nodes` or `subnodes`: read as them, but write `text` and `children`. |

---

<!-- docs/recipes.md -->

# Recipes

How to use Orbit with common frameworks and tools. Every map fills its container, so give the container a height.

- [Plain HTML](#plain-html)
- [React and Next.js](#react-and-nextjs)
- [Vue](#vue)
- [Svelte](#svelte)
- [Astro](#astro)
- [Markdown pipelines](#markdown-pipelines)
- [Static sites, emails and print](#static-sites-emails-and-print)

## Plain HTML

The `<orbit-map>` element needs no build step:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { defineOrbitMapElement } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@restless-dreams/orbit/+esm';
  defineOrbitMapElement();
</script>

<orbit-map height="420">
  # 🚀 Project

  ## Research <!-- orbit status: active -->
  ## Build
  ## Launch
</orbit-map>
```

Hide elements until the script loads, so the raw markdown never flashes: `orbit-map:not(:defined) { visibility: hidden; }`.

To draw into your own element instead:

```js
import { createOrbitMap } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

const map = createOrbitMap(document.querySelector('#map'), markdown, { theme: 'auto' });
map.on('focus-change', ({ node }) => console.log(node.text));
```

## React and Next.js

`@restless-dreams/orbit/react` is marked `"use client"`, so you can render it from a Server Component. It draws a static SVG of the map on the server, and the live map takes over in the browser.

```tsx
// app/roadmap/page.tsx (a Server Component)
import { OrbitMindMap } from '@restless-dreams/orbit/react';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

const RoadmapPage = async () => {
  const markdown = await readFile('content/roadmap.md', 'utf8');
  return (
    <div style={{ height: 520 }}>
      <OrbitMindMap source={markdown} theme="auto" />
    </div>
  );
};

export default RoadmapPage;
```

Callbacks are functions, which can't cross from a Server Component, so put interactive maps in a client component:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { OrbitMindMap, type OrbitMindMapRef } from '@restless-dreams/orbit/react';

export const RoadmapExplorer = ({ markdown }: { markdown: string }) => {
  const map = useRef<OrbitMindMapRef>(null);
  const [focusedId, setFocusedId] = useState<string>();

  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={() => map.current?.overview()}>Show everything</button>
      <div style={{ height: 520 }}>
        <OrbitMindMap
          ref={map}
          source={markdown}
          focusedId={focusedId}
          onFocusChange={(node) => setFocusedId(node.id)}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
};
```

## Vue

Use the web component. Tell Vue that `orbit-map` is a custom element:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue';

export default {
  plugins: [vue({ template: { compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag === 'orbit-map' } } })],
};
```

```ts
// main.ts
import { defineOrbitMapElement } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

defineOrbitMapElement();
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';

const markdown = ref('# Project\n\n## Research\n## Build');
const focused = ref('');
</script>

<template>
  <orbit-map
    :source="markdown"
    height="420"
    @orbit-focus-change="(event) => (focused = event.detail.node.text)"
  />
  <p>Looking at: {{ focused }}</p>
</template>
```

Setting `source` redraws the map and keeps the reader's place.

## Svelte

An action draws the map and redraws it when the markdown changes (Svelte 4 and 5):

```svelte
<script>
  import { createOrbitMap } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

  let { markdown } = $props();

  const orbit = (element, source) => {
    const map = createOrbitMap(element, source);
    return {
      update: (next) => map.render(next),
      destroy: () => map.destroy(),
    };
  };
</script>

<div use:orbit={markdown} style="height: 420px"></div>
```

## Astro

Interactive, with the web component:

```astro
---
import markdown from '../content/roadmap.md?raw';
---
<orbit-map source={markdown} height="420"></orbit-map>

<script>
  import { defineOrbitMapElement } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';
  defineOrbitMapElement();
</script>
```

Or static, with no JavaScript at all:

```astro
---
import { renderToSVGString } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';
import markdown from '../content/roadmap.md?raw';
const svg = renderToSVGString(markdown, { responsive: true, theme: 'paper' });
---
<figure style="height: 420px" set:html={svg} />
```

## Markdown pipelines

**marked:** `@restless-dreams/orbit/marked` turns ```` ```orbit ```` fences into maps (see [Markdown pipelines](guide.md#markdown-pipelines-marked) in the guide).

**remark and rehype** (Astro, Docusaurus, Next.js MDX, Eleventy, …): a small rehype plugin replaces the fences with static SVG at build time:

```js
import { visit } from 'unist-util-visit';
import { toString } from 'hast-util-to-string';
import { fromHtml } from 'hast-util-from-html';
import { renderToSVGString } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

/** Replaces ```orbit code blocks with a static SVG of the map. */
export const rehypeOrbit = (options = {}) => {
  return (tree) => {
    let count = 0;

    visit(tree, 'element', (node, index, parent) => {
      const code = node.tagName === 'pre' ? node.children.find((child) => child.tagName === 'code') : null;
      const classes = code?.properties?.className ?? [];

      if (!code || !classes.includes('language-orbit') || !parent || index === undefined) {
        return;
      }

      count += 1;
      const svg = renderToSVGString(toString(code), { responsive: true, idPrefix: `orbit-${count}`, ...options });
      parent.children[index] = fromHtml(svg, { fragment: true, space: 'svg' }).children[0];
    });
  };
};
```

To make those maps explorable in the browser, emit `<orbit-map>` elements instead of SVG and load `defineOrbitMapElement()` on the page.

## Static sites, emails and print

`renderToSVGString` and the `orbit render` command draw a map without a browser:

```bash
npx @restless-dreams/orbit render roadmap.md --out roadmap.svg --theme night --width 1600 --height 1000
npx @restless-dreams/orbit render roadmap.md --view all --out overview.svg
```

The SVG has its colors resolved and its labels as text, so it opens the same in browsers, design tools and image converters. Give each SVG inlined in one page its own `idPrefix`.

---

<!-- docs/theming.md -->

# Theming

## Themes

![The fourteen themes: paper, night, glass, glass night, cosmos, blueprint, ink, contrast, flat, flat night, material, material night, liquid and liquid night](media/themes.webp)

| Theme | Looks like | Background |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `paper` (default) | Pastel planets with a soft colored shadow and a fine rim of their own color | Your page's |
| `night` | Luminous planets that glow on a deep navy sky | Its own |
| `glass` | Frosted, translucent planets with a bright rim | Its own pastel backdrop |
| `glass-night` | Tinted glass planets that glow over an aurora | Its own |
| `cosmos` | Jewel-toned planets lit from one side, around a golden star with a corona | Deep space with stars |
| `blueprint` | Outlined planets, construction lines and monospaced labels | A gridded blue sheet |
| `ink` | Black line art: outlined planets, a black sun and serif lettering | Your page's |
| `contrast` | Black outlines, solid colors and bold labels, for the most legible map | White |
| `flat` | Solid, saturated planets with white lettering: no shading, shadows or glow | Your page's |
| `flat-night` | Bright solid planets with dark lettering, cut out from the page | Near black |
| `material` | Material 3: tonal containers around a sun in the primary color (see [Material themes](#material-themes-from-any-color)) | A tonal surface |
| `material-night` | Material 3's dark scheme: deep containers with light lettering | A dark tonal surface |
| `liquid` | Liquid glass: clear planets that catch the light along their rims | A vivid wallpaper of its own |
| `liquid-night` | Liquid glass at night, glowing in each planet's color | A deep, vivid wallpaper |
| `auto` | `paper` or `night`, following the reader's light or dark preference | |

Choose one with the `theme` option, the `theme` attribute of `<orbit-map>`, the `theme` prop in React, or `theme:` in a map's frontmatter.

Your own themes get a name too: `registerTheme('brand', { preset: 'night', tokens: { … } })` makes `theme: brand` work in all of those places (see [Extending](extending.md#themes)). The same guide covers status words with your own colors and node types with their own look.

Labels keep at least 4.5:1 contrast with their node in every theme (WCAG AA), on every branch color, every shade below it and whichever node is in focus; `contrast` keeps more than 7:1 (AAA).

## Material themes from any color

`materialTheme(color)` builds a Material 3 theme from one color, the way Material You colors an app from its wallpaper: tonal palettes in the color's hue, surfaces and containers chosen by tone, the sun in the primary color and each branch in its own hue, spread evenly around the color wheel from yours. Colors are chosen by tone, so labels and text stay readable whatever the color.

```ts
import { createOrbitMap, materialTheme, registerTheme } from '@restless-dreams/orbit';

createOrbitMap(element, markdown, { theme: materialTheme('#0B57D0') });

// Or name it, for `theme: brand` in frontmatter and <orbit-map theme="brand">:
registerTheme('brand', materialTheme('#E11D48', { dark: true }));
```

It takes any color Orbit reads (hex, `rgb()`, `oklch()`…) and returns a theme object built on `material`, or `material-night` with `{ dark: true }`. The `material` themes themselves are built from Material's baseline purple, `MATERIAL_SEED`.

## Custom properties

Everything a theme sets is a CSS custom property. Set them on the map's container, or anywhere above it, to restyle a map from your own stylesheet; they win over the theme:

```css
.roadmap {
  --orbit-font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  --orbit-color-root: #ffd166;
  --orbit-color-1: #ef476f;
  --orbit-color-2: #06d6a0;
  --orbit-color-3: #118ab2;
  --orbit-focus-ring: #ef476f;
}
```

For `<orbit-map>`, set them on the element (`orbit-map { --orbit-surface: … }`); they pass into its shadow root.

| Group | Properties |
| --- | --- |
| Fonts | `--orbit-sans-font`, `--orbit-serif-font`, `--orbit-mono-font` (the page's font of each kind, which themes draw with: see [Fonts](#fonts)), `--orbit-font-family` (the map's own font, for its controls and sheet, and by default its labels) |
| Page | `--orbit-surface` (background color), `--orbit-surface-pattern` (CSS background layers drawn over it, or `none`), `--orbit-text`, `--orbit-muted-text` |
| Node colors | `--orbit-color-root`, `--orbit-color-1` … `--orbit-color-7` (one per top-level branch, in order), `--orbit-shade-light` and `--orbit-shade-dark` (what deeper nodes are mixed toward) |
| Planets | `--orbit-node-fill-opacity`, `--orbit-moon-opacity`, `--orbit-node-highlight` (the lit side), `--orbit-node-terminator` (where light turns to shadow), `--orbit-node-shading` (the far edge), `--orbit-node-shade-circle` (where the shading spreads, see below), `--orbit-note-indicator` |
| Rims | `--orbit-node-stroke`, `--orbit-node-stroke-tint`, `--orbit-node-stroke-width` (in pixels; in a crowded orbit, a planet's rim is 4% of its radius per pixel, so it grows and shrinks with it), `--orbit-badge-stroke` (around status dots and content markers, which grow with their nodes) |
| Shadow or glow | `--orbit-node-shadow`, `--orbit-node-shadow-tint`, `--orbit-node-shadow-opacity`, `--orbit-node-shadow-offset`, `--orbit-node-shadow-size`, `--orbit-sun-shadow-opacity`, `--orbit-sun-shadow-size` |
| The sun's halo | `--orbit-sun-halo`, `--orbit-sun-halo-tint`, `--orbit-sun-halo-opacity`, `--orbit-sun-halo-width`, `--orbit-sun-halo-dash`, `--orbit-sun-halo-size` |
| Orbits | `--orbit-ring-stroke`, `--orbit-ring-tint`, `--orbit-ring-opacity`, `--orbit-ring-width`, `--orbit-ring-dash` |
| Lines (overview) | `--orbit-link-stroke`, `--orbit-link-tint`, `--orbit-link-opacity`, `--orbit-link-width`, `--orbit-link-dash` |
| Labels | `--orbit-label-font`, `--orbit-display-font` (the node in focus and the detail sheet's title), `--orbit-label-weight`, `--orbit-display-weight`, `--orbit-label-letter-spacing`, `--orbit-root-text`, `--orbit-node-text`, `--orbit-node-text-inverse` (on dark nodes), `--orbit-label-shadow` (behind light labels) |
| Focus | `--orbit-focus-ring` |
| Controls | `--orbit-control-background`, `--orbit-control-border`, `--orbit-control-text`, `--orbit-control-muted-text`, `--orbit-control-active-background`, `--orbit-control-active-text`, `--orbit-control-shadow`, `--orbit-control-blur` |
| Tooltip | `--orbit-tooltip-background`, `--orbit-tooltip-text` |
| Content buttons | `--orbit-action-background`, `--orbit-action-border`, `--orbit-action-text`, `--orbit-action-shadow` |
| Detail sheet and media viewer | `--orbit-sheet-background` (behind the viewer's media too), `--orbit-sheet-text`, `--orbit-sheet-muted-text`, `--orbit-sheet-border`, `--orbit-sheet-backdrop`, `--orbit-sheet-shadow` (under the viewer's videos too), `--orbit-sheet-blur`, `--orbit-chip-background`, `--orbit-chip-text`, `--orbit-link-text`.
